MINUTES OF A REGULAR MEETING OF THE LOMITA CITY COUNCIL
  December 3, 2012

1. OPENING CEREMONIES

  a. Call Meeting to Order

A regular meeting of the Lomita City Council was called to order at 7 p.m. on Monday,
December 3, 2012, in the Council Chambers, Lomita City Hall, 24300 Narbonne Avenue.

  b. Flag Salute

Councilmember Traina led the salute to the flag.

  c.  Invocation

Councilmember Sanchez gave the invocation.

  d. Roll Call

Those responding to roll call by Assistant City Clerk Shumway were COUNCILMEMBERS:
Gazeley, Savidan, Traina, Sanchez, and Mayor Estrada. Also present were City Manager Rock,
Assistant City Manager Sugano, City Attorney Hogin, Community Services Director McPherron,
Public Works Director Damasse, Parks and Recreation Director Harding, Administrative
Services Director Chavez, and Assistant City Clerk Shumway.

2. APPROVAL OF AGENDA

Councilmember Gazeley moved to approve the agenda. Councilmember Sanchez seconded
the motion, which carried unanimously.

3. CITY MANAGER’S REPORT

City Manager Rock reported that the City's Utility Division staff estimated that about 1,600
customers had been overbilled on their water bills due to meter reading days being extended
beyond the typical billing cycle, which in turn pushed some water users into a higher rate tier.
According to City Manager Rock, normally water meter readings are conducted approximately
every 60 days, but due to the integration of the new water meter reading system, the meter
reading period had been extended. City Manager Rock added that customers will be credited
between the range of $5.00 and $7.00, and the total amount to be credited to customers by the
City is not expected to exceed $12,000. City Manager Rock concluded by reassuring residents
and the City Council that future water meter reading would be conducted approximately every
60 days.

  Page 1 of 9
 4. ORAL COMMUNICATIONS AND MEETING ATTENDANCE REPORTS FROM THE CITY
  COUNCIL

Mayor Gazeley congratulated Narbonne High School's Varsity Football Team on winning the
City Championship and advancing to the State playoffs.

Councilmember Savidan asked that a resolution in support of sequestration be placed on the
next City Council agenda. Councilmember Sanchez seconded that motion, which carried
unanimously.

Councilmember Savidan requested that the creation of an ad hoc subcommittee to look into
increased issues of helicopter noise in Lomita be agendized for a future City Council meeting.
City Attorney Hogin advised City Council to defer discussion of that request until Agenda Item 7,
Organizational Assignments for Councilmembers.

Councilmember Traina thanked City Manager Rock for his clarification on the water billing
issues, and stated that he had received several calls from residents regarding increases in their
last water bill; in fact, Councilmember Traina stated that he also saw a slight increase in his own
water bill due to being placed in a different tier. Continuing with the issue of water billing,
Councilmember Traina stated upon reviewing his water bills for the last five years, he found that
his rates had increased 52.8%, which is different than the 48% increase indicated by staff when
water rates were reviewed earlier in 2012. Furthermore, Councilmember Traina pointed out that
the 3% increase in water rates in March 2012, was not included in the staff report or brought up
by staff during the water rate review. Councilmember Traina requested that staff better inform
the public regarding rates, increases, issues with billing, etc.

Councilmember Traina also asked that recognition of the Narbonne High School Varsity Football
Team be placed on the agenda of the next City Council meeting. The Council agreed with
Councilmember Traina.

Councilmember Sanchez informed those in attendance that the Community Emergency
Response Team (CERT) training has been scheduled for April 2013, and that exact dates will be
announced shortly.

Mayor Estrada reminded residents that the Household Hazardous Waste Collection Day is
currently scheduled for Saturday, December 15, 2012, from 9 a.m. to 3 p.m., and will take place
in the City Hall parking lot.

5. ORAL COMMUNICATIONS

Susie Dever, Member of the Railroad Museum Foundation Board, invited the City Council to the
Museum Appreciation Party, which was being held for all donors, Friends of the Lomita Railroad
Museum, volunteers, and Railroad Museum staff. Board Member Dever also provided a
schedule for upcoming Railroad Museum Speaker Events.

Sharon Houston, Lomita resident, stated that she received her water bill on November 15, 2012,
even though the meter reading was done on August 9, 2012; Ms. Houston questioned why it
took so long to mail the water bill. Ms. Houston added that other water departments bill on a

  Page 2 of 9
 monthly basis, and suggested that the City look into implementing monthly water billing. City
Manager Rock responded that water meters will be read every 60 days.

Veronica Hurtado, Representative of the Lomita Chamber of Commerce, provided an update
regarding the Chamber's most recent Business Mixer at Kaiser Permanente, and thanked City
Manager Rock and Councilmember Gazeley for attending. Ms. Hurtado also informed those in
attendance that the next Business Mixer is currently scheduled for December 5, 2012, at 5:30
p.m., and will take place at the Kiwanis Club.

George Kivett, Lomita resident, congratulated the Narbonne High School Varsity Football Team.
Mr. Kivett also stated that he would like to see more publicity for events at the Railroad Museum,
which in turn would bring more people to the area. Finally, Mr. Kivett stated that he was happy
that an ad hoc subcommittee regarding helicopter noise would be created, since the noise is
becoming an issue.

6. CONSENT AGENDA

Councilmembers Traina and Sanchez asked that Item 6.I. be pulled for discussion.
Councilmember Traina moved to approve the Consent Agenda, minus Item 6.I. Councilmember
Savidan seconded the motion, which carried unanimously.

Regarding Item 6.I., Councilmember Sanchez suggested increasing the lease term for the
Sharp Copier, from 36 months to 48 months, in an effort to save more money with a longer term
lease. Discussion followed on whether purchasing a copier would be cheaper than leasing one,
and what would be the most cost efficient for the City. Councilmember Traina moved to
authorize the City Manager to enter into a lease agreement for up to 48 months.
Councilmember Gazeley seconded the motion, which carried unanimously.

  a. Motion to Waive Further Reading.

  b. Recommendation to approve the minutes for the City Council Meeting held on November
  19, 2012. RECOMMEND APPROVAL.

  c. Approval of Demands. RECOMMEND APPROVAL.

  d. Monthly Report for Economic Development and Information Technology activities.
  RECEIVE AND FILE.

  e. Monthly Report for the Parks and Recreation Department. RECEIVE AND FILE.

  f. Monthly Report for the Administrative Services Department. RECEIVE AND FILE.

  g. Monthly Treasurer’s Report. RECEIVE AND FILE.

  h. Award of a Public Works Agreement to FS Construction in the amount of $67,150, for the
  Crenshaw Blvd. and Lomita Blvd. Intersection improvements (Phase 1). RECOMMEND
  APPROVAL.

  i. Approval of a Lease for a Sharp Copier for a 36 month term. RECOMMEND APPROVAL.
  Page 3 of 9
   SCHEDULED MATTERS

7. WORKFORCE INVESTMENT BOARD APPOINTMENT

  Assistant City Manager Sugano stated that the City had received an application for the
  Workforce Investment Board from Chandler Call. Councilmember Gazeley made a motion
  to appoint Chandler Call to the Workforce Investment Board. Councilmember Sanchez
  seconded the motion, which carried unanimously.

  Chandler Call thanked the City Council for his appointment to the Workforce Investment
  Board. David Gonzales, Executive Director of Pacific Gateway, also thanked the City
  Council for the appointment of Mr. Call to the Workforce Investment Board, and provided
  informational brochures to Council about the program. Mr. Gonzales added that the main
  goal of the various workforce investment programs are to get people back to work.

8. CYPRESS WATER PRODUCTION FACILITY (CWPF) OFFLINE TESTING STATUS
  UPDATE, BLIND TASTE TESTING, AND PUBLIC OUTREACH

  A. Blind Taste Testing
  B. Presentation of Water Quality Data Results from Hazen and Sawyer
  C. Authorize staff to proceed with preparation to reactivate CWPF, with a target date
  of mid-February 2013, to distribute water to customers
  D. Authorize staff to proceed with the Public Education and Outreach Program for
  reactivation of CWPF

  Lynn Grijalva, Consultant from Hazen and Sawyer, stated that throughout the past month
  Hazen and Sawyer staff, along with City staff, had been conducting water testing at the
  Cypress Water Production Facility (CWPF), and making various adjustments to water
  production in order to achieve good quality water at the CWPF.

  Members of the public, along with the City Council and staff, took part in the blind water
  taste testing.

  Ms. Grijalva provided a PowerPoint presentation while the results of water taste testing were
  tabulated. Ms. Grijalva informed those in attendance that in accordance with Title 22, the
  well water must be tested every two years, and based on the test results, the City of
  Lomita's well water meets all regulatory limits, except for manganese, which is removed to a
  “non-detectable” level when well water is treated at the CWPF. According to Ms. Grijalva,
  based on a review of the lab results, the following conclusions can be made: the taste and
  odor associated with the well water were the result of sulfide organics, and deposits found in
  the well water came from calcium carbonate. Ms. Grijalva noted that Public Works' staff had
  made a number of improvements to CWPF since 2010, including replacing piping located
  along Pacific Coast Highway, adding a connection for Metropolitan Water District (MWD)
  water or for blending purposes, and adding an aeration system for enhanced mixing within
  the reservoir.

  Ms. Grijalva stated that the results of the well water testing met all the goals established by
  the City Council prior to testing (i.e., hardness, total dissolved solids, and palatable taste).
  Page 4 of 9
 Based on well water testing and analyses conducted by Hazen and Sawyer, Ms. Grijalva
stated that the long-term recommendations are as follows: 1) continue adjusting chlorination
throughout the year to maintain a residual of 2.5 - 3.5 mg/l; 2) continue aeration to promote
enhanced mixing inside the reservoir and; 3) continue blending, as well as making
operational adjustments, in order to meet water quality goals, and to prevent corrosion and
deposits. Ms. Grijalva concluded her presentation by stating that the next step of the
process would be to initiate a community outreach program.

Following her PowerPoint presentation, Ms. Grijalva presented the results of the blind water
taste testing conducted prior to the presentation. According to Ms. Grijalva, of those tested
earlier in the evening, 43% indicated their preference for Metropolitan water, while 34%
preferred the 50/50 blend of MWD and well water, and only a quarter of those tested
identified Metropolitan water as the water they currently receive from their household water
taps.

Public Works Director Damasse recommended that City Council accept the water quality
results presentation from Hazen and Sawyer, and requested City Council to authorize the
Public Works Department to proceed with the preparation of the CWPF and related water
facilities for reactivation with a target date of mid-February 2013 for distribution of blended
water to Lomita customers. Director Damasse also requested authorization from City
Council to allow staff to direct Hazen and Sawyer to commence with the Public Outreach
Program.

Councilmember Traina requested that staff provide details regarding the projected
operational costs for the CWPF, including all expenses such as salaries, energy costs, etc.
City Manager Rock responded by stating that the cost of operating the CWPF would only be
an approximate cost at this time, as the CWPF has never been fully operational, so true
costs would not be known for some time.

Councilmember Traina inquired as to whether the water testing was performed only at the
CWPF or at various sites. Public Works Director Damasse responded that the City is
required to sample water from different locations, of which there are currently 6 sample
stations.

In response to Councilmember Sanchez’s questions regarding pH levels and LSI, Ms.
Grijalva stated that both Ph and LSI levels are within an acceptable range, as well as levels
for water hardness. Discussion followed on how often the water sampling and testing would
be performed.

Joe McGrath, Lomita resident, stated that he was disappointed that the 3.5% increase in
water rates, which took place in March 2012, was not publicly noted. Mr. McGrath also
asked City Council to consider lowering water rates if there are savings anticipated with
initiating the water blending process at the CWPF. Mr. McGrath went on to state his
concern with several issues related to the blending process, including potential damage to
water heaters, proximity of the CWPF to a landfill, and deficiencies associated with the
elevation of the water tank. Mr. McGrath also inquired as to when Council will hear a
presentation from WaterWorks, as was previously requested and approved to be on a future
agenda.

  Page 5 of 9
 George Kivett, Lomita resident, stated that Chandler Call was an excellent person to be
appointed to the Workforce Investment Board. In terms of the proposed water blending at
CWPF, Mr. Kivett stated that his main concern with the blended water is water hardness.

Rob Friedrich, Lomita resident, also expressed his concern with the proximity of CWPF to
the landfill. Mr. Friedrich inquired as to whether any mercury was detected in the water.

Sharon Houston, Lomita resident, suggested that the City should start out with 50/50 blend
of well water and Metropolitan water, which would provide better quality water to residents.
Ms. Houston also requested that residents be allowed to go to reservoir and do water
tasting there.

Dave Albert, Lomita resident, was glad to see that Council was coming together. Mr. Albert
also expressed his concern with the aging water distribution system.

Marty Spain, Lomita resident, requested that Council review water rates and distribute
savings to water customers.

Ms. Grijalva responded to some of the questions and concerns from the public; those
responses are as follows:

  •  The water blending system was run at full capacity in order to be representative of
  water production rates. The water tank was run all the way to the bottom during
  testing, and the tank could be drained all the way down. The water levels in the tank
  could be raised higher in order to get the aeration that they need for mixing. Staff
  purchased clear water pitchers, which were used during the water taste testing, so
  that the public could see and compare water clarity.
  •  In order to test for water residue in water heaters, staff heated water heaters at the
  CWPF to different temperatures and those water heaters were running all the time.
  •  Both staff and consultants paid close attention to water hardness, and searched for
  various solutions to lower hardness as much as possible. Tests were conducted for
  measuring organics in the well water, which is also a requirement of Title 22, and the
  results of the tests did not detect any pollution to the water from the nearby landfill.
  Anytime there is a change of piping in a distribution system, it allows for better flow
  and better water quality, so the replacement of the water line on PCH improved both
  water flow and quality. The problem of water quality could be associated with the old
  water distribution system, and therefore it is important to replace aged distribution
  systems over time.
  •  The collection of data was witnessed by Hazen and Sawyer and laboratory results
  were provided directly to Hazen and Sawyer, as well as emailed to Public Works
  Director Damasse.
  •  In regards to water hardness, the goal was identified to meet a range of 180 - 250,
  mg/L which was approved by City Council and provided to Hazen and Sawyer.

Public Works Director Damasse provided the following comments:

  •  Mercury was undetected in water testing, which spanned five different testing times
  since 2010. The City has received some complaints over the past year that some
  Page 6 of 9
   private piping damage is from well water provided from the treatment plant. Well
  water or blended water has not been distributed to customers since 2010, and
  currently residents are getting only MWD water.
  •  General piping corrosion probably due to age, in which some of the pipes are over 30
  years old. During water testing, staff used different processes to blend water from
  different zones, with higher elevation blending improving water quality.

  City Manager Rock stated that the PCH water line was replaced earlier this year, the water
  lines on Eshelman Avenue would be replaced next year, and in the future more CIP projects
  will be brought forward for replacing the City’s aging water distribution system.

  In response to Dave Albert's question, City Manager Rock stated that different approaches
  to water blending were utilized, as compared to water blending in 2010, when blending was
  performed by more simply running water for a long period of time. According to City
  Manager Rock, current water blending includes operational improvements, such as
  aeration, the mixing of water, and changing the percentages of the blending ratio.

  Councilmember Traina requested that the Council consider adding the following two items to
  staff’s recommendations:  1) schedule a public meeting to discuss how savings
  accumulated as a result of the water blending process would be utilized by the City; and 2)
  for City Manager to provide on a bi-monthly basis a report regarding complaints received
  and how those complaints were resolved.

  Discussion followed on when the true operational costs of the CWPF would be known.
  Councilmember Sanchez stated that City Council would be revisiting both water rates and
  tiers in the future, as was previously directed by Council.

  Councilmember Traina made a motion to approve staff’s recommendations as indicated in
  the staff report, as well as the two additions he stated earlier regarding the discussion of
  cost savings and a report on complaints received and how they were resolved. Motion died
  for lack of a second.

  Councilmember Savidan made a motion to approve Item 8 as recommended by staff.
  Councilmember Sanchez seconded the motion.

  ROLL CALL:
  AYES: Councilmembers Savidan, Sanchez, Gazeley, and Mayor Estrada.
  NAYS: Councilmember Traina.

9. ON-LINE REGISTRATION FOR RECREATION CLASSES AND ACTIVITIES

  Parks and Recreation Director Harding provided an overview of the staff report. Director
  Harding stated that the cost of processing payments online, a convenience fee, would be an
  additional 6.5% of the normal class price, and would only be charged to online registrants.
  According to Director Harding, ActiveNet would charge the City a one-time fee of $1,300,
  which would be for to the installation of the online registration module and this fee would be
  the only associated cost to the City.

  Councilmember Gazeley moved to approve the online registration module for recreation
  Page 7 of 9
   classes and activities.  Councilmember Traina seconded the motion, which carried
  unanimously.

10. ADULT “BIG BALL” SOFTBALL LEAGUE

  Parks and Recreation Director Harding provided an overview of the staff report. Director
  Harding stated that one of the past issues was too many home runs, so in an effort to lessen
  that issue, the size of the ball is much larger, which in turn will make it harder for players to
  hit the ball over the fence.

  Mayor Estrada suggested to end games at 9 p.m., in order to eliminate potential complaints
  about noise.

  Councilmember Gazeley moved to approve the adult softball league.  Councilmember
  Sanchez seconded the motion, which carried unanimously.

11. GOLF TOURNAMENT NET PROCEEDS DISTRIBUTION

  Parks and Recreation Director Harding provided overview of the staff report. Director
  Harding recommended that the golf tournament net proceeds be distributed as follows:
  $5,500 for the Teen Program, $3,000 for the Youth Golf Program, and $4,000 for the Youth
  Basketball Program.

  Mayor Estrada moved to approve the distribution of the golf tournament proceeds as
  indicated in the staff report. Councilmember Gazeley asked City Council whether they
  would consider giving some of the money to the Lomita Little League. Responding to
  Councilmember Gazeley’s question, City Attorney Hogin clarified current procedure for the
  distribution of funds to youth organizations, which require such organizations to submit a
  written request for funds that are to be reviewed by Council during budget time. City
  Attorney Hogin added that this procedure allows for the fair distribution of funds to
  organizations and programs. Councilmember Savidan seconded the motion, which carried
  unanimously.
